title: latent-harmonizer-continuous-batcher-queue-damping
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: Continuous batching under mixed-priority workloads occasionally allowed persistent low-priority starvation and mid-tail latency spikes when KV cache pins and kernel selection conspired to form micro-pipelines of long-running requests. This PR introduces the 'latent harmonizer', a lightweight queue-damping and timeout orchestration layer that smooths admission bursts, enforces soft fairness credits, and moves a small set of KV-cache pin heuristics into the scheduler to reduce cross-request interference. Changes: 1) scheduler: add soft-fairness credit accounting with exponential decay and a configurable damping factor to prevent bursty priority inversion; 2) queueing: introduce per-cohort enqueue jitter and time-horizon backoff to spread arrival peaks and reduce coalescer monopolization; 3) timeouts: tighten soft-reservation timeouts and add a probe lease that opportunistically preempts stalled slots when backlog and age thresholds are exceeded; 4) KV cache: add pin-eligibility window tracking and a lightweight sampler-driven demotion path to avoid long-term KV pin starvation; 5) kernels: add hints to kernel selector for short-seq fast-path preference when harmonizer detects high churn; 6) observability: new metrics for harmonizer_credit, cohort_damping, kv_pin_age_buckets and an internal histogram for preempted_slot_age. Performance: in internal bench runs with mixed chat+embedding workload the harmonizer reduced 99th percentile generation latency by 18-28% in contention scenarios and lowered effective token cost by 6% due to fewer wasted kernel warmups. Testing: unit tests for credit decay and enqueue jitter, e2e contention tests and KV pin demotion tests added; canary rollout plan described below. Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag runtime.harmonizer.enabled=false by default; staged rollout to Dedicated then Hosted with automatic fallback; add console knobs for damping_factor and probe_threshold. Risk and mitigation: risk of over-preemption causing throughput regression fixed by conservative defaults and a safety circuit that disables harmonizer when preemption_rate > 0.5% for 5m; added alerts and automatic rollback in console. See linked Linear tickets for experimental traces and benchmark dashboards. Checklist: code, unit tests, integration tests, docs, bench results, ops runbook, canary plan.

release_notes: Operational: New runtime feature 'latent harmonizer' to reduce continuous-batcher tail latency and prevent starvation; default disabled. Operators: damping_factor and probe_threshold knobs added to runtime config; recommended conservative defaults documented. Observability: new metrics harmonizer_credit, cohort_damping, kv_pin_age_buckets. Rollout: staged canary with automatic rollback conditions described in ops runbook.
ci_logs_summary: Batcher unit tests: pass; e2e contention suite: pass after one flaky run fixed; bench harness: shows 18-28% 99p reduction in contested scenarios; lint: pass; integration: pass.
manual_testing_notes: Local bench reproducibility: run tools/bench/bench_continuous_batcher.py --profile=contended_mixed_load --runs=50; verify harmonizer_credit metric and kv_pin_age_buckets shift; validate canary flag toggling via runtime config.
operational_runbook: 1) Enable runtime.harmonizer.enabled=false->true in 10% of nodes. 2) Monitor harmonizer_credit and preemption_rate for 15m. 3) If preemption_rate > 0.5% or 99p latency regresses >5% rollback automatically. 4) Tune damping_factor down if throughput drops. 5) For KV-heavy services increase pin_eligibility_window_ms cautiously.
